title: Taking 1:1 instead of 2:1 on the same NQ rule took the win rate from 35% to 51% and finished $19,000 lower
author: person-person12
selftext:
Every time I post a win rate under 40% somebody tells me to just take 1:1 and stop being greedy, so I ran the same rule twice and changed only where the target sits.

The rule: NQ 15 minute candles, 50 candle average, take the first close back across it either way, stop 1 ATR, flat at 15:55. One contract from $50,000, May 2016 to March 2026, commission and slippage charged on both sides of every trade. Same candles, same entries, same stop. The only difference between the two runs is the target at 1 ATR against 2 ATR.

**Target 2 ATR:** 4,176 trades, **35.37% wins**, profit factor 1.04, finished at $101,354, worst drawdown 51.9%.

**Target 1 ATR:** 4,515 trades, **50.52% wins**, profit factor 1.03, finished at $82,330, worst drawdown 35.1%.

The win rate did exactly what people say it will, 35% to 51% off one change, and **it cost $19,024 of the final balance to buy.**

**\_\_\_\_\_**

The part I didnt expect is the drawdown. Cutting the target took the worst drop from 51.9% to 35.1%, which on a funded account is the difference between dead and still trading. Both versions land on basically the same profit factor, 1.04 against 1.03, so theyre earning about the same per dollar risked and just packaging it differently.

The trade count moved too, 4,176 up to 4,515, because a closer target gets filled on candles where the further one turned around and came back to the stop. That also means the 1:1 version paid more in fees, $45,150 against $41,760, and it still ended with the shallower hole.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

Fair part, id want somebody to say this if it was my post being taken apart. Neither of these is worth trading, profit factor 1.03 over 4,515 trades is a coin flip you paid fees on. I changed the target on one rule on one instrument, so this is not a general law about risk reward, and somebody running a trend continuation instead of an average reclaim could get the opposite result. Both runs sit in my [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) account with every one of those trades listed if anyone wants a specific year pulled out.

What I can say off this one is that the 1:1 version finished 19 grand lower, won 15 points more of its trades, and held 17 points less drawdown while doing it.
